trace: A student types a question in the Gradio interface.
respond checks the current message before calling the local model.
An allowed message reaches generate; a blocked request skips model generation.
The output is checked and a metadata-only JSON log line is written.
Monitoring aggregates allowed-request latency and all-request block counts.
diagrams.explanation: Deployment turns a model into a system that accepts requests and returns usable answers. In this lab, Gradio calls the Python respond function directly. The separate FastAPI exercise offers another route to the same model; the Gradio interface does not call that API. respond first applies an input check to the current message. Allowed requests combine a system instruction, recent history and cleaned text, then generate returns answer text and token counts. A basic output check runs before the answer is returned. Blocked requests skip generation and receive a refusal. Both paths write latency, model identity, token counts and the blocking reason to a JSON-lines log. Monitoring summarises those records into percentiles and counts. These simple pattern checks illustrate the flow; they do not guarantee that every injection or personal-data format will be detected.
diagrams.check_question: Does a blocked request consume model-generation tokens in respond?
diagrams.check_answer: No. It skips generate and logs zero prompt and completion token counts for that request.

trace: The SDK sends 'Name two uses of FastAPI.' to the local endpoint.
ChatRequest parses messages and max_tokens; the endpoint caps output length.
generate formats messages into tokens and waits for the shared model lock.
Only generated continuation tokens are decoded as the assistant answer.
The response includes choices and a usage block for the SDK to read.
diagrams.explanation: An API is an interface through which one program requests work from another. The OpenAI-compatible exercise receives an HTTP request containing JSON fields. FastAPI uses ChatRequest to parse the body, and chat_completions passes its messages to generate. The chat template adds the role markers expected by the model, while the tokenizer converts the formatted text to token IDs. MODEL_LOCK prevents the notebook and server from generating on the shared model simultaneously. The model's output includes the original input prefix plus its continuation. generate slices away that prefix, decodes only new tokens and reports input and output counts. The endpoint packages those results into choices and usage fields. Compatibility concerns this response structure; the lab endpoint remains a small demonstration without the authentication, streaming or complete request controls of a deployed service.
diagrams.check_question: Why are prompt and completion token counts returned separately?
diagrams.check_answer: They describe different work: reading the input and producing the answer. They support usage and cost calculations.

Observe batching throughput separately from single-request latency.
Inspect which simulated requests were blocked or redacted and compare p50 with p95.
diagrams.explanation: The lab begins with streaming measurements before introducing serving. measure times the first non-empty decoded text chunk, an approximation of first-token latency because a chunk can contain several tokens. The FastAPI exercise then exposes generation to a client program. monthly_cost uses classroom prices, while retry simulation illustrates delayed retries after rate limiting. The efficiency experiments distinguish different tradeoffs: fake_quantize approximates low-bit weights but restores them as floating-point tensors, so the size table is theoretical; batching measures aggregate throughput; caching reuses an answer for a repeated message list. The Gradio application calls respond directly, adding simple checks and log records. Finally, synthetic traffic produces a monitoring summary. The generated Docker files are a smaller packaging scaffold, so compare their features with the notebook before assuming equivalent application behaviour.
diagrams.check_question: Does fake_quantize reduce the actual model tensor storage to four bits in this experiment?
diagrams.check_answer: No. It rounds then dequantises weights into floating-point tensors. The size estimate describes hypothetical packed low-bit storage.

glossary.meaning: A URL and request handler through which a program exposes an operation.
The elapsed time needed to serve a request.
Work completed per unit time, such as total generated tokens per second.
Time to first token; this lab approximates it with first non-empty decoded text.
Representing weights with a limited set of values, often to store fewer bits.
Processing several inputs together in one model operation.
Stored results reused when an equivalent request returns.
A latency value at or below which roughly 95% of measured requests fall.

pitfalls: Higher batching throughput does not automatically mean lower latency for every individual user.
The notebook's fake quantisation size estimates do not describe actual packed tensor memory.
The Gradio path and FastAPI path are separate exercises; input checks in respond do not protect the API endpoint.
